author: WP07
summary: An orientation map of the core framework and graphics API (math, Game/content, graphics resources, model and stock effects, GraphicsDevice and state objects, Effect base and queries) with one boundary per row. Mostly current, but stale at TARGET on GameWindow (platform facade, not SDL3-bound), the content ladder (.cnb tier), state objects (shared payload, immutable once bound), compiled-effect families (nine options) and Model scratch state. The site had the behaviour spread across guide pages but no single map; it is now a reference deep dive linking every row to its owning page.

sections.heading: Core Framework and Graphics API Reference

concepts.section: Core Framework and Graphics API Reference
concepts.text: The quick reference groups overload families instead of reproducing declarations: the module-owned headers remain the signature authority and behavioural pages own the qualifications.

concepts.section: Core Framework and Graphics API Reference
concepts.text: A listed method proves API presence only; it does not imply that each of the 21 implementation families renders it with the same semantics.
concepts.note: Family count taken from the TARGET canon instead of the book macro.

concepts.text: Vector2/3/4 expose public components, constants, arithmetic, distance/dot, interpolation, normalisation, reflection and transforms (Vector3 adds cross); value-returning and output-reference overloads are separate API rows needing separate tests.
tokens: output-reference overloads are separate API rows

concepts.text: Matrix keeps XNA's row-vector convention; the CNAEXT ToColumnMajor(float[16]) is a marked bridge for shader upload, not a change of convention.
Quaternion multiplication order and normalisation are behavioural contracts, not naming details.
Point and Rectangle use integer screen coordinates and XNA/FNA's exact edge, empty and intersection rules.

Color is a packed AABBGGRR value; it derives from the polymorphic IPackedVector interface so its object is not its four-byte stream form, and constructor argument types change overload choice and clamping.

Plane, Ray and the bounding types translate C# nullable returns to std::optional (Ray::Intersects returns std::optional<float>) and out parameters to output references; compare semantics, not signature strings.

Math value semantics, coordinate and vertex-layout conventions are covered by the math guide and math module internals; generated XNA XML is useful inventory but needs language normalisation and behavioural oracles.
concepts.note: Cross-reference to pages that already own the math detail.

concepts.text: Game exposes lifecycle events, components, content, services, window and device, fixed/variable timing and Run/Tick/Exit plus the hooks; host ownership differs by platform and the call order is the contract.
tokens: the call order is the contract

concepts.text: GameTime carries total and elapsed time plus the slow-frame flag and is written only by Game; user code consumes the snapshot.

The appendix says CNA uses one SDL3-backed GameWindow; at TARGET GameWindow is one concrete facade delegating to the selected platform's IPlatformWindow (SDL3, SDL2, X11, Wayland, Win32, Headless or Terminal) where FNA uses per-platform subclasses.

GraphicsDeviceManager stores preferred back-buffer, depth, profile and full-screen settings, ApplyChanges and device events; stored presentation values are requested state, not proof the driver accepted them; the default profile is Reach.

ContentManager resolution: the appendix says XNB first, then a registered loose reader; at TARGET .xnb, then CNA's compiled .cnb, then per-type loose readers (.cnj and native formats); Load<T> returns by value.
Path resolution, the XNB container/object graph and CNJ are separate routes; success on one is not evidence for another, and caching/ownership vary by asset type.
tokens: success on one route is not evidence for another

concepts.text: Texture2D offers dimensions/bounds, whole and rectangular SetData/GetData, FromStream, SaveAsPng/SaveAsJpeg (plus CNAEXT file-name overloads and DDSFromStreamEXT).
A Texture2D round trip can observe CNA's CPU shadow rather than sampled GPU memory, and mip/sub-rectangle behaviour is renderer-specific.
Texture3D and TextureCube construction, format, mip, upload and readback are separate capabilities with no universal CPU fallback; volumes are refused under Reach.
RenderTarget2D/RenderTargetCube binding, preserve/discard, multiple targets, cube unbind and readback are independent renderer paths.
Vertex/IndexBuffer dynamic intent, upload hint, CPU shadow and renderer buffer are four distinct layers.

SpriteBatch Begin/End, Draw overloads and DrawString (strings and StringBuilder): sort mode, state objects, custom effect, transform and clipping must each reach the renderer; a visible sprite does not prove every argument.
tokens: a visible sprite does not prove every argument

concepts.text: SpriteFont (atlas, glyph/cropping/character/kerning arrays, spacing, default character, measurement) enters through different XNB, CNJ and hand-built reader and ownership routes.
Detailed texture, render-target and SpriteBatch behaviour and the implementation-family matrix live on their own pages; do not infer cross-renderer guarantees from the common C++ type.
concepts.note: Cross-reference to the owning guide pages.

concepts.text: Model::Draw requires every part effect to implement IEffectMatrices (InvalidOperationException otherwise) and uses a static thread_local scratch array for absolute bone transforms, so calls on one thread are serial.
concepts.note: Refined: the scratch state is per thread.

concepts.text: Model, ModelBone, ModelMesh and ModelMeshPart expose bone/mesh collections, hierarchy, transform-copy helpers, part buffers/declarations, effects and draw; several loading routes have different provenance.
BasicEffect: matrices, texture and vertex colour, material colours, fog and three lights; which fields are consumed is decided by each renderer's shader mapping.

AlphaTestEffect: a renderer without a discard path must refuse rather than draw opaque (PORTABLEGL refuses a non-default alpha test); the appendix's 'fallback loses alpha test' shape no longer applies to current 3D renderers.
tokens: PORTABLEGL refuses a non-default alpha test by name

target.evidence: PortableGLRenderer.cpp (refuse("an alpha test")); IGraphicsRenderer default fallback only inherited by 2D/STUB families

concepts.note: Corrected: no current 3D family inherits the effect-discarding fallback.

concepts.text: DualTextureEffect's second layer needs a second UV set in the vertex layout and a renderer route.
EnvironmentMapEffect's cube construction/sampling and effect dispatch are separate gates; lighting cannot be turned off.
SkinnedEffect: 72-bone palette, 1/2/4 weights, CNAEXT vertex-colour addition; palette and layout are run-time contracts.
Model runtime ownership, glTF/CNJ import and the glTF evidence matrix are documented on the model pages.

GraphicsDevice is the renderer-independent facade with groups for identity/profile/presentation, resource and target binding, scalar and object state, clear/present/readback, draw families (bound, user-array, indexed, instanced, CNAEXT indirect), capabilities and the unsupported-3D policy.
The facade stores and returns state even where a family does not consume it; SupportsCapability(...) == true is a preflight hint, not an execution result.
The four state objects: BlendState (factors, functions, four write masks, blend factor, multisample mask), DepthStencilState, RasterizerState, SamplerState.

The appendix says CNA copies assigned state objects by value; at TARGET copies share one payload (reference semantics), binding marks it bound, later setters on any copy throw InvalidOperationException and reassigning the bound object is a no-op.
tokens: Cannot modify a BlendState after it has been bound to a GraphicsDevice
concepts.note: Corrected: shared payload and bind-time immutability, as in XNA.

concepts.text: Whether each state-object field reaches native state still depends on the renderer family.
tokens: still depends on the renderer family

concepts.text: Effect owns parameter and technique collections, a current technique, Clone and the CNAEXT Apply; the byte constructor works where CompiledEffects is true — FNA3D always and nine families behind options (the appendix lists eight).

EffectParameter exposes typed setters/getters, class/type/dimension metadata, elements, members and annotations; on stock effects the records are CNA-built and only compiled parameters are reflected storage.
The Effect byte route is not a source compiler and refuses .fx/HLSL, DXBC and MGFX; ShaderEffect is a distinct route, and a stock effect or parameter setter never proves compiled-effect execution.

OcclusionQuery exposes Begin, End, IsComplete, PixelCount and CNAEXT isPixelCountPreciseEXT(); construction throws NotSupportedException under Reach, with the capability false or when the renderer creates no query.
A non-null query object and a true capability are insufficient without a discriminating sample-count test, because some renderers report only a 0/1 flag.

Exact declarations live under modules/<owner>/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/ (CNA-only extensions under include/CNA/, CNAEXT markers on XNA-namespace additions); pair each header with implementation, renderer route, tests and host evidence.
The representation census (331/331 types, 3,627/3,627 members) measures presence, not behaviour.
The appendix answers 'where is the surface?'; the behavioural pages and audit records answer 'what does this revision do?'.
